We are advised by the members of the Commission that none of them have received campaign contributions within the last twelve months.
The applicant or any property owner entitled to notice of the hearing may, within fifteen days after the date of the Planning Commission decision, appeal the Planning Commission decision to the City Council (Ord. No. 091-529). A fee is required for filing an appeal with the City Clerkâ€™s office (R05-14).
The Council may, within fifteen days after the date of the decision or on or before the first date following the first Council meeting after the date of the Planning Commission decision, whichever occurs last: 1) Confirm the action of the Planning Commission and grant or deny the application; 2) Set the matter for public hearing and dispose of it in the same manner as on an appeal; or 3) Amend, modify, delete or add any condition of approval which the Council finds is not substantial under the circumstances relative to or affecting the property subject to the application for a development entitlement. Any determination of the Council pursuant to this paragraph shall be conclusive and final.
The Planning Commission reserves the right to modify the order of items shown on the agenda and advises all interested parties to arrive promptly at the commencement of the meeting.

MINUTES OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES,
  CALIFORNIA

  February 16, 2016

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was
called to order by Chair Thomas at 6:33 p.m. on February 16, 2016, in the City Council
Chambers, 340 Palos Verdes Drive West, Palos Verdes Estates, California. The Pledge of
Allegiance followed.

ROLL CALL

Present:  Kao, Evans, Hunter, Welch, Chair Thomas

Absent:  None

Also Present: Planning Director Sheri Repp-Loadsman; City Planner Elizabeth Corpuz;
  Assistant City Attorney Gregg Kettles; Julie Cremeans, Minutes Secretary

  *  *  *

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

None.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Chair Thomas, upon confirmation the applicants present understood the suggested conditions of
approval, opened the public hearing, confirmed that there were no interested persons wishing to
voice concerns regarding the application considered for the Consent Calendar, and closed the
public hearing.

9.  M-1075-15; Consideration of a Miscellaneous Application for an accessory structure
  exceeding the allowable height at the single family residence located at 3821 Via
  Palomino. Lot 2, Block 6218, Tract 6887. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to
  California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant/Owner:  Tres & Julie Reid

MOTION

  Commissioner Welch moved to approve M-1075-15 for 3821 Via Palomino, exempt
from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution PCR-2016-0903
with standard conditions. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Evans and was carried by
unanimous oral vote.

Planning Commission  1  February 16, 2016
 OLD BUSINESS

1.  WT-130-15; Wireless Telecommunication Facilities Application for new equipment
  within the City right-of-way on the corner of Via Fernandez and Via Visalia.

  Applicant:  Crown Castle NG West LLC
  300 Spectrum Center Dr., #1200
  Irvine, CA 92618

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Steven Garcia (Crown Castle NG West LLC, 300 Spectrum Center Drive, Irvine) came forward
and presented the application.

Commissioner Evans asked about the ground equipment options, and Mr. Garcia responded that
the applicant presented what it determined to be the lest intrusive means.

Michael Warter (1959 Via Visalia) came forward speaking against options A and B, which are
eyesores.

Mr. Garcia re-approached and pointed out that option C seems to be the preferable choice.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Planning Director Repp-Loadsman noted that the title on record will change.

MOTION

  Commissioner Hunter moved to approve WT-130-15 for new equipment within the City
right-of-way on the corner of Via Fernandez and Via Visalia., exempt from CEQA and subject to
the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution PCR-2015-0869 with standard conditions and
the following additional conditions: 1) The steel pole shall be burnished prior to painting. The
pole and antennas must be painted a flat dark brown, and maintained in the same condition
thereafter; 2) The CISH equipment cabinet should be painted dark green to blend in with the
existing surrounding environment and nearby meter cabinets in the public right-of-way; 3)
Crown Castle shall place its name on the lid of the proposed equipment vault; 4) All cables
interconnecting the antennas and all transmission equipment should run within the replacement
pole except as minimally required to connect to the antennas; 5) The replacement steel pole is
not a wireless tower for any purpose, but rather it is considered only a replacement City street
sign pole; 6) The steel pole shall be designated as a replacement for the existing pole to be
removed, and after installation, the replacement pole shall be dedicated to the City for a fee of
$1.00 so that it is clear for federal law purposes that replacement pole maintain its primary use
and function as a City traffic sign support; 7) Permittee shall install and at all times maintain in
good condition an “RF Notice” and “Network Operations Center Information” sign on the steel
pole at approximately 14 feet AGL; 8) Permittee shall ensure that all RF signage complies with
FCC OET Bulletin 65 or ANSI C95.2 for color, symbol, and content conventions; 9) Attached
street signs shall be installed in accordance with the MUTCD (Manual Uniform Traffic Control
Devices) California Edition; and 10) Attached street signs shall be with approved hardware per

Planning Commission  2  February 16, 2016
 the City’s Maintenance Foreman. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Kao and was
carried by unanimous oral vote.

2.  WT-145-15; Wireless Telecommunication Facilities Application for new equipment
  within the City right-of-way across from 801 Via Coronel.

  Applicant:  Crown Castle NG West LLC
  300 Spectrum Center Dr., #1200
  Irvine, CA 92618

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Commissioner Hunter asked about options to place the support cable further away for the
pedestrians, and Jonathan Kramer (2001 S Barrington Ave, Los Angeles) came forward and
advised that the cable has to be in line and can’t be moved.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Steven Garcia (Crown Castle NG West LLC, 300 Spectrum Center Drive, Irvine) came forward
and presented the application.

Deborah Fox (1616 Cataluna Place) came forward and suggested that conditions be added to this
and every similar application to minimize the size of the equipment box and require that Crown
Castle come back annually and report on any new technologies that would allow reduction in the
size of the equipment box.

Maryellen Semel (2200 Chelsea Road) came forward and commented that Crown Castle’s
revisions are a big improvement.

Camille Feldman (1713 Chelsea Road): came forward with concerns about runners tripping on
the support cable and asking that it be moved for aesthetic reasons as well.

Dale Sanchez (744 Cloyden Road) came forward and asked that the poles and antennas be
removed, pointing out that they don’t have any in Rancho Palos Verdes and asking that the area
be kept rural.

Fred Robertshaw (1725 Chelsea Road) came forward and also expressed his concern about the
safety issue with the support cable, asked about the study addressing service coverage and
advocated using wooden mockups so that the residents are clear that it’s a mockup and not an
existing pole that they can’t do anything about.

Katie Sobie (1817 Via Estudillo) also came forward with concerns about health and safety and
asked why so many towers are proposed within this small geographic area.

Mr. Garcia re-approached and addressed the concerns that were raised, pointing out that: 1) there
would be no need for annual inspections of a solution that has already been identified; 2) the
applicant has no preference for the style of mockups; 3) the guide wires are required elements of
that existing pole and has always been there; 4) visibility was taken into consideration, and the
pole has been moved back and the configuration changed; 5) Crown Castle has more than 100
sites in Rancho Palos Verdes; 6) there has been an analysis process with an independent

Planning Commission  3  February 16, 2016
 consultant review; 7) the Crown Castle facilities are always compliant, which is verified by
City’s independent consultant.

Discussion ensued between the Commission and Mr. Garcia regarding the guide wire,
technology improvements, similar designs and configurations in Rancho Palos Verdes, future
applications expected by other carriers and possible collocation, and costs of installation.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioner Evans asked about the overall plan for the 22 sites and the City’s process, and
Planning Director Repp-Loadsman advised the Commission and audience of what is being done
to give the community a better understanding of what’s being proposed. Planning Director
Repp-Loadsman also commented that she will post Mr. Kramer’s presentation on the website.

Commissioner Evans asked about an annual review as part of the conditional use permit process,
and Mr. Kramer advised against compelling the applicant to do anything about any changes in
technology before the expiration of a 10-year permit.

Commissioner Evans asked about health and safety concerns, Mr. Kramer gave an overview of
the safety standards, and Chair Thomas advised that the issue is not within the scope of the
Planning Commission.

Commissioner. Evans asked for Mr. Kramer’s opinion on the recommendations, and Mr. Kramer
discussed State code for down guides and pointed out that there would be no increase in potential
harm and that there would be a decrease by following Code and putting guide markers at the
bottom.

Commissioner Welch asked whether a map of the overall project is available to the public, and
Planning Director Repp-Loadsman responded that it is in the public files at City Hall and offered
to place the map on the City’s website.

Commissioner Welch commented that this seems like the least intrusive method and agreed with
the need for the additional coverage.

Commissioner Evans appreciated the appropriate comments from the residents and Mr. Kramer’s
expertise and commented that this is the right solution for this location.

Commissioner Hunters and Kao agreed.

Chair Thomas commented that these are not things that are welcomed in the neighborhood, but
the process has found the least intrusive means for the need at this location.

MOTION

  Commissioner Hunter moved to approve WT-145-15 for new equipment within the City
right-of-way across from 801 Via Coronel., exempt from CEQA and subject to the conditions as
provided in Planning Resolution PCR-2015-0890 with standard conditions and the following
additional conditions: 1) The DAS nodes shall not be located on the pole and shall be located
within a ground mounted CISH-51 cabinet; 2) The cantenna must be painted a flat dark brown,
and maintained in the same condition thereafter to match the existing wood pole; 3) All cables
interconnecting the antennas and all transmission equipment should run vertically flush to the

Planning Commission  4  February 16, 2016
 existing wood pole, except as minimally required to connect to the antennas; 4) The equipment
cabinet should be painted a color to blend in with the existing surrounding environment and
nearby meter cabinet in the public right-of-way; 5) Permittee shall install and at all times
maintain in good condition an “RF Notice” and “Network Operations Center Information” sign
on the wood pole at approximately 3 feet below the cantenna; and 6) Permittee shall ensure that
all RF signage complies with FCC OET Bulletin 65 or ANSI C95.2 for color, symbol, and
content conventions.. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Evans and was carried by
unanimous oral vote.

3.  NC-1541/G-1559/M-1053/M-1066-15; Consideration of Neighborhood Compatibility,
  Grading & Miscellaneous Applications for a new single family residence located at 2812
  Victoria Place. Lot 16, Block 2450, Tract 7332. This project is exempt from CEQA
  pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Rosa Velazquez
  118 S. Catalina Ave., #N
  Redondo Beach, CA 90277

  Owner:  Ebrahim Soltani

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Commissioner Kao asked about drainage requirements, and City Planner Corpuz discussed the
two options given to the applicant and pointed out that a full grading plan has not yet been done.
Planning Director Repp-Loadsman added that there is an obligation through the Homes
Association but no legal mechanism to enforce it. The neighbors generally work collaboratively
with each other.

Commissioners Welch and Hunter: asked about setbacks, and Chair Thomas asked about the
pool deck silhouette, and City Planner Corpuz provided details.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Rosa Velazquez (designer at 118 Catalina Avenue, Redondo Beach) came forward and presented
the application.

Extensive discussion ensued between the applicant and the Commissioners.

Walter Christmas (3028 Via Buena), Bizhan Khaleeli (representing the owners of 2806 Via
Victoria), Leven Leatherbury (2729 Palos Verdes Drive West), Jeanne and Fikret Atamdede
(2818 Victoria Place) and Lauren Cotner (222 Avenida Del Norte, Redondo Beach) came
forward and raised concerns with mass, scale, safety, privacy, looming and landscaping.

Ebrahim Soltani (applicant) came forward and commented that the city is on a hill with greenery
and shrubs being major factors for privacy, and he is working with the neighbor to ensure that
the fence and greenery will be put in for privacy.

Commissioner Welch asked about the amount of fill, and Ms. Velazquez provided details.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Planning Commission  5  February 16, 2016
 Commissioner Hunter asked about approving the house without the deck, and Planning Director
Repp-Loadsman advised that the Commission could approve a portion of the application.

Commissioner Hunter then commented that the applicant has made changes to address privacy
concerns. Progress has been made, but there are still issues around the raised deck and changes
can be made to mitigate the privacy concerns of the neighbors. Commissioner Hunter advised
that he is comfortable with the house but not the deck as designed or adding walls that are not in
the plans or silhouetted.

Commissioner Kao commented that it is a workable plan with impacts from house mitigated, but
the back yard is the main issue, which doesn’t seem difficult to remedy.

Commissioner Evans agreed that the privacy issue from the house was solved, but it exacerbated
the issues from the deck

Commissioner Welch commented that the architect has done a fantastic job addressing the
privacy concerns with the house, but something can be done in regard to the patio.

Chair Thomas added that in addition to concerns about the deck, he has concerns with the
unintended consequences of the additional ridge height.

MOTION

  Commissioner Thomas moved to approve in part NC-1541/G-1559/M-1053/M-1066-15
for 2812 Victoria Place, exempt from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in
Planning Resolution PCR-2015-0853 with standard conditions and the following additional
conditions: 1) A license agreement shall be submitted to defend, indemnify, and hold harmless
the city, its officers, agents and employees from and against any and all loss, damage, liability,
claims, demands, costs, charges, and expenses, including attorney’s fees, and causes of action of
whatsoever character which the City may incur, sustain or be subjected to on account of loss or
damage to property or loss of use thereof, or for bodily injury to or death of any person arising
out of or in any way connected to the encroachment; 2) A license agreement shall be submitted
to reimburse the City for any costs incurred by the City to repair damage, restore premises, or
satisfy claims incurred by reason of the encroachment; and 3) The entire outdoor patio area and
deck are denied. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Evans and was carried by
unanimous oral vote.

Planning Director Repp-Loadsman explained that the applicant will need to submit a Revised
Neighborhood Compatibility application and new Grading Permit application for any proposed
outdoor patio/deck improvements.

4.  NC-1543/G-1560/M-1064/M-1065-15; Consideration of Neighborhood Compatibility,
  Grading & Miscellaneous Applications for a new single family residence located at 709
  Via Somonte. Lot 11, Block 1538, Tract 6884. This project is exempt from CEQA
  pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant/Owner: GA Design Inc.

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Planning Commission  6  February 16, 2016
 Mahmoud Gharachedaghi (architect at GA Design Architecture and Planning, 19191 S. Vermont
Avenue, #640, Torrance) came forward and presented the application.

Chair Thomas asked about lowering the garage plate height, and Mr. Gharachedaghi responded
that lowering the plate height of the garage means lowering the first level, increasing grading and
burying the first floor more underground.

Commissioner Welch asked how the first floor elevation compared to the current home
elevation, and Mr. Gharachedaghi responded that it is 2’8” lower.

Alvaro Lundy (representing Elaine Bohner at 793 Via Somonte) came forward and discussed the
view impact.

Rick Bohner (793 Via Somonte) came forward and discussed the building and tree heights and
requested a tree height restriction as condition of approval.

Colleen Nazari (789 Via Somonte) came forward and discussed the view impacts.

Carol Gregory (816 Via Somonte) came forward and commented that the application does not fit
with the location.

Fred Gregory (816 Via Somonte) came forward and commented that it is a large house jammed
in on small lot and impacting privacy and views. It does not meet neighborhood compatibility
and wills et a bad precedent.

Mr. Gharachedaghi re-approached and commented that he met with the neighbors several times
and changed the building design after each neighbor and Commission meeting.
Mr. Gharachedaghi compared the application to other houses in the neighborhood and discussed
the changes requested and made.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Chair Thomas asked about landscape screening, and Planning Director Repp-Loadsman advised
that the Commission has the ability to add conditions, but City Council has cautioned to
minimize them as they are difficult to enforce.

Commissioner Kao commented that application needs to be viewed as it is today against
neighborhood standards, and it is incompatible. It is still too high in probably the most view
sensitive area in the city, and more can be done.

Commissioner Evans commented that this is the fourth meeting and the applicant did lower the
ridgeline by changing the roof pitch, but the changes have been minimal. Privacy, view and
massing concerns should have all been addressed by the applicant.

Commissioner Welch commented that he is ready to approve the application but is not pleased
with it and concerned with the Art Jury process. The applicant has done everything reasonable
and practicable on a contrasting slope with a neighbor at an elevation that is close to 30 feet
higher, and there is precedent where the rights of a second story versus the rights of a view do
come out on the side of the second story. There is no obliteration of views.

Planning Commission  7  February 16, 2016
 Commissioner Hunter commented that this applicant came in with an unreasonable application,
went through four contentious meetings and now has something close to reasonable. There is
less than a 5 percent impact to a spectacular 180 degree panoramic view. There are concerns
about overall mass of the house, but there is no path that allows the project to move forward.
Bringing the entire site down another foot would be a fair and reasonable compromise.

Chair Thomas commented that the Commission has to look at where the project ended up, not
where it started, and whether everything reasonable and practicable has been done to mitigate
impacts on the neighbors. Not everything has been done, but it could be approved with a
condition that it come down by one more feet and a condition for landscape screening no higher
than the eaves.

Commissioner Welch commented that he can’t support the additional foot of excavation.
Commissioner. Kao commented that he can support it. Commissioner Hunter agreed that the
landscaping is an important condition to add. Commissioner Evans commented that it would be
a step in the right direction but would still be a massive project that’s one foot lower in the
ground and incompatible with the neighborhood.

Commissioner Welch asked what is massive about the project, and Chair Thomas responded that
it has a high floor area ratio on a small lot. Commissioner Welch then commented that the
Commission is not in the business of designing homes and the envelope of the project seems
reasonable, and the application is approvable as presented.

MOTION

  Chair Thomas moved to approve NC-1543/G-1560/M-1064/M-1065-15 for 709 Via
Somonte, exempt from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution
PCR-2015-0859 with standard conditions and the following additional conditions: 1) The non-
standard encroachments shall not be located within the first 5-feet behind the curb; 2) 6-inch
curb gutter shall be installed along the property frontage. A curb and gutter plan shall be
prepared by a Registered Civil Engineer; 3) A license agreement shall be submitted to defend,
indemnify, and hold harmless the city, its officers, agents and employees from and against any
and all loss, damage, liability, claims, demands, costs, charges, and expenses, including
attorney’s fees, and causes of action of whatsoever character which the City may incur, sustain
or be subjected to on account of loss or damage to property or loss of use thereof, or for bodily
injury to or death of any person arising out of or in any way connected to the encroachment; 4) A
license agreement shall be submitted to reimburse the City for any costs incurred by the City to
repair damage, restore premises, or satisfy claims incurred by reason of the encroachment; 5)
The overall ridge height of the residence shall be reduced by 1 ft.; and 6) Landscaping shall not
exceed the height of the roof ridgeline. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Hunter and
was carried 3-2 with Commissioners Welch and Evans dissenting.

5.  NC-1539/G-1557/M-1079/M-1080-15; Consideration of Neighborhood Compatibility,
  Grading & Miscellaneous Applications for a new single family residence located at 2101
  Chelsea Road. Lot 6, Block 2100, Tract 7331. This project is exempt from CEQA
  pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Cauthen Design Inc.
  20141 E. Chapman Ave.
  Orange, CA 92869

Planning Commission  8  February 16, 2016
   Owner:  Kirby & Sally Larson

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Ben Cauthen (architect at 20141 E. Chapman Avenue, Orange) came forward and presented the
application.

Discussion ensued among Mr. Cauthen and the Commission regarding the wall, the garage and
the plate heights.

Louis Zakin (2112 Chelsea Road) came forward to discuss neighborhood compatibility. It is a
massive project with impacts on views of the mountains, oceans and coastal cities, and it will
significantly affect property values.

George Richards (2100 Chelsea Road) came forward to discuss the size and height of the
application.

Clark Kasunich (2108 Chelsea Road) came forward to discuss view blockage.

Mr. Cauthen re-approached and commented that the application is more than compatible with the
neighborhood and that Mr. Kasunich would only be able to keep his view if it was a single-story
house.

Commissioner Welch asked whether the applicant had considered having the height of the newly
built house on Paseo Del Mar be his maximum height, and Mr. Cauthen responded that did not
but did compare the finished floor and finished grade.

Commissioner Welch and Mr. Cauthen then discussed driveway approach options.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioner Welch commented that the applicant made a strategic decision to wait until the
home at 2100 Paseo del Mar was built, so it is reasonable that it should be at that same height.
Also, there should be a 25-foot driveway approach.

Commissioner Hunter commented that he is not ready to approve yet and agrees that there is
room on the height and that the driveway should be brought down. The scale of the house is not
an issue. The chimneys stick up quite a bit, serve no purpose and are intrusive into the views.
Also, two of the most affected neighbors are not available to be at the meeting.

Commissioner Kao commented that the height is still an issue, and he has concerns about the
overall size of the structure, as a matter of perspective, from Chelsea going northbound.

Commissioner Evans commented that it needs more study. The average size in the area is one-
third of the size of this project. Some of the mass should be moved to ground level to preserve
views and spread out the property on the large lot. It’s not compatible with the neighbors on
Chelsea.

Planning Commission  9  February 16, 2016
 Chair Thomas agreed with reducing the driveway and bringing the ridge down. However,
changing the chimneys would change the nature of the fireplace inside the house.

Mr. Cauthen accepted a 90-day extension.

CONTINUED TO THE MARCH 15, 2016, PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING

6.  M-1067-15; Consideration of a Miscellaneous Application for an accessory structure
  exceeding the allowable height at the single family residence located at 3819 Via La
  Selva. Portion of Lot T, Tract 6887. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to
  California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Tomaro Architecture
  2617 N. Sepulveda Blvd., #100
  Manhattan Beach, CA 90266

  Owner:  Javier & Jenna Martinez
  4733 Torrance Blvd., #121
  Torrance, CA 90503

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Louis Tomaro (architect at 2617 N. Sepulveda Boulevard, Manhattan Beach) came forward and
presented the application.

Commissioners Kao and Evans and Mr. Tomaro discussed the pool location, plate height and
roof slope.

Tom Funk (3925 Via Picaposte) came forward and discussed the changes from the original plans
and his concerns about noise and the fence and the pool house exceeding building code.
Mr. Funk requested noise mitigation efforts.

Mr. Tomaro re-approached and discussed relocation attempts and the agreement to build a new
8-foot fence for privacy.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

The Commission and Staff discussed changes to the height of the pool house and pool deck.

Commissioner Welch commented that this looks like a challenge for the architect with the Art
Jury.

Commissioner Hunter commented that this is the second and third bite of the apple and not a fair
way to handle the applications. The deck should be brought down.

Commissioner Kao commented that he would like to see the height of the pool house lowered to
achieve what was originally approved and to mitigate impacts to the neighbors.
